_howto: This is what you author. Everything else - ticket text, agent briefs, tracker payloads - is rendered from it by emit.py. Fill it in phase order, delete this key, then run validate.py. See assets/examples/example-bundle.json for a complete one.

story.source_text: PHASE 1: the original ask, verbatim. Scope creep is detected against this.

tracker_meta._howto: PHASE 1, first: copy what the tracker already says, verbatim. Labels are decisions somebody made before you opened this - 'production-issue' means it escaped to customers, 'sev1' means refinement is the wrong instrument right now. Never invent a label, and never edit one to make a rule match. This is also what stops a push from deleting the labels somebody set.

triage._howto: PHASE 1: written by `triage.py apply --bundle bundle.json --write`. Do not hand-write it; if the labels are wrong, fix the ticket, and if the policy is wrong, fix triage.labels in refinery.yaml.

intake._howto: PHASE 1: run `intake.py assess --bundle bundle.json --write`, then read source_text and set heuristic:false on every dimension you confirm. Statuses: present (quote it) | missing (blocking question) | assumed (assumption + non-blocking question) | answered (answer + answered_by).
intake.domain_rationale: PHASE 1: Cynefin. clear (known practice) | complicated (knowable, needs expertise) | complex (only knowable by probing - the output is a spike, not a plan) | chaotic (act first, refine later). Say why in one arguable sentence.

impact._howto: PHASE 1, when the ask names a mechanism with no outcome, or whenever the goal is worth stating: goal -> actor -> impact -> deliverable. Fill it right to left if you have to, but the goal is what tells you afterwards whether this worked.
impact.goal: measurable, with a number and a date

story.summary_human: PHASE 6: why and what, within the word budget.
story.technical_notes_human: PHASE 6: what changes, where, what was decided. Every path cited.

decision_table._howto: PHASE 3, for rule-heavy stories. List the conditions and every value each can take; write one rule per combination, using "*" for any. Anything the system cannot reach goes in 'impossible' with a reason. validate.py enumerates the product and names what neither covers (DT001) - that is the hole an implementer would otherwise fill by guessing. Delete this block for stories that are not rule-driven.

non_goals: PHASE 3: what this story is not, with follow-up ticket ids.

risks._howto: PHASE 4: from the premortem. It is three months later, this shipped and caused an incident - write the postmortem, then record each cause here. 'detection' is the alert, metric or report that tells you it is happening; a high risk without one is a risk you hear about from a customer.

non_functional._howto: PHASE 3: a quality attribute scenario ends in a response measure. performance, concurrency and failure need a number or the word 'unchanged' (NFR002); the rest may be categorical, but never blank.
non_functional.performance: e.g. checkout p95 stays under 400ms at 500 rps, or 'unchanged'

decisions.question: PHASE 4: an open technical fork.
decisions._howto_deferred: PHASE 4: when status is 'deferred', add 'waiting_for' (the information that would decide it) and 'expires' (the event or date after which deferring costs more than deciding - the last responsible moment). Real Options: an option without an expiry is not a held option, it is an unmade decision.

sources: PHASE 2: which of index / manifest / scan produced this

subtasks.title: [repo] Verb object
subtasks.human: PHASE 6: within the word budget, assumes shared context.

forbidden: Do not edit files another subtask owns.
agent_brief.context_budget_hint: read_first only; do not index the repo

review._howto: PHASE 8: once validate.py is green, run `review.py brief --bundle bundle.json --out reviews/` and hand each sealed packet to a separate critic in fresh context. Record what they found here, resolve every finding, re-validate, then `review.py digest --bundle bundle.json --stamp`.
review.bundle_digest: PHASE 8: written by `review.py digest --stamp`. Never typed by hand.

critics.attempted: only when this critic raised nothing: what it tried to break, and why it held

findings.claim: what is wrong, in one sentence
findings.failure: who does what, and what they wrongly get, if this ships as is
findings.resolution: what changed. accepted -> the risk and who accepted it; disputed -> the rebuttal and its evidence
